relevance_reason: Reports patients from two families with complex I deficiency caused by NDUFV2 mutations (MC1DN7), including a novel frameshift and Leigh syndrome phenotype.

findings.statement: Cameron et al. (2015) reported 2 sibs with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and brain atrophy who were diagnosed with mitochondrial complex I deficiency based on low enzyme activity in muscle and a high lactate/pyruvate ratio in fibroblasts.
quotes: Two siblings with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and brain atrophy were diagnosed with Complex I deficiency based on low enzyme activity in muscle and high lactate/pyruvate ratio in fibroblasts.

phenotypes.text: decreased complex I activity in muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

findings.statement: In 2 sibs with complex I deficiency, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and brain atrophy, Cameron et al. (2015) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the NDUFV2 gene, found by whole-exome sequencing of fibroblast DNA from one sib and filtering for novel nonsynonymous changes: a previously reported intronic splice mutation (c.IVS2+1delGTAA), considered disease causing, and a novel 1-bp insertion (c.669_670insG) predicted to cause a frameshift (p.Ser224Valfs*3).
quotes: Two compound heterozygous mutations were identified in both siblings in NDUFV2, encoding the 24 kDa subunit of Complex I.

The intronic mutation (c.IVS2 + 1delGTAA) is disease causing and has been reported before. The other mutation is novel (c.669_670insG, p.Ser224Valfs*3) and predicted to cause a pathogenic frameshift in the protein.

findings.statement: Cameron et al. (2015) reported a consanguineous family in which 3 of 5 sibs with complex I deficiency presented with Leigh syndrome but without cardiac involvement.
quotes: In this family three of five siblings were affected. Interestingly, they presented with Leigh syndrome but no cardiac involvement.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

findings.statement: By screening of 10 probands with complex I deficiency from different families, Cameron et al. (2015) identified homozygosity for the NDUFV2 intronic c.IVS2+1delGTAA mutation in a consanguineous family with Leigh syndrome.
quotes: Subsequent investigation of 10 probands with complex I deficiency from different families revealed homozygosity for the intronic c.IVS2 + 1delGTAA mutation in a second, consanguineous family.

findings.statement: Cameron et al. (2015) noted that homozygosity for the c.IVS2+1delGTAA NDUFV2 mutation had previously been reported in 2 families presenting with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, truncal hypotonia, and encephalopathy, whereas their family with the same genotype had Leigh syndrome without cardiac involvement, expanding the clinical phenotype associated with this mutation.
quotes: The same genotype had been reported previously in a two families but presenting with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, trunk hypotonia and encephalopathy.
The diagnosis of Leigh syndrome expands the clinical phenotypes associated with the c.IVS2 + 1delGTAA mutation in this gene.

relevance_reason: Only the abstract is available. It describes screening 8 complex I nuclear genes, among them NDUFV2 and NDUFS4, in 8 patients with isolated complex I deficiency and finding molecular defects in 3 patients. The abstract does not say which genes or variants were involved.

findings.statement: Pagniez-Mammeri et al. (2009) screened 8 patients with biochemically proven isolated mitochondrial complex I deficiency for mutations in 8 nuclear complex I genes (NDUFS1, NDUFS2, NDUFS3, NDUFS4, NDUFS7, NDUFS8, NDUFV1, and NDUFV2). They used Surveyor nuclease digestion of 22 cDNA fragments covering the coding sequences. Single-nucleotide polymorphisms and missense mutations were detected in 18.7% of the cDNA fragments, and molecular defects were identified in 3 patients.
quotes: Eight complex I nuclear genes, among the most frequently mutated (NDUFS1, NDUFS2, NDUFS3, NDUFS4, NDUFS7, NDUFS8, NDUFV1 and NDUFV2), were studied in 22 cDNA fragments spanning their coding sequences in 8 patients with a biochemically proved complex I deficiency.
Single nucleotide polymorphisms and missense mutations were detected in 18.7% of the cDNA fragments by Surveyor nuclease treatment. Molecular defects were detected in 3 patients.

findings.statement: Pagniez-Mammeri et al. (2009) concluded that Surveyor nuclease screening of cDNAs is a reliable and easy-to-interpret way to genotype nuclear complex I deficiencies, and that it reduces the number of sequencing reactions needed. They suggested that the method would make prenatal diagnosis more feasible.
quotes: Surveyor nuclease screening is a reliable method for genotyping nuclear complex I deficiencies, easy to interpret, and limits the number of sequence reactions. Its use will enhance the possibility of prenatal diagnosis

relevance_reason: First report of an NDUFV2 mutation causing complex I deficiency with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and encephalopathy.

findings.statement: Bénit et al. (2003) described 3 affected sibs from a consanguineous family who had complex I deficiency with early-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and trunk hypotonia. The authors noted that this cardiomyopathy contrasted with the mainly neurologic symptoms seen with mutations in most other complex I subunit genes.
quotes: causes complex I deficiency and early onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with trunk hypotonia in three affected sibs of a consanguineous family
this first mutation in NDUFV2 is strikingly associated with cardiomyopathy

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

findings.statement: In 3 affected sibs from a consanguineous family with complex I deficiency and early-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, Bénit et al. (2003) used denaturing HPLC and sequencing to identify a homozygous 4-bp deletion in intron 2 of the NDUFV2 gene (IVS2+5_+8delGTAA). The deletion altered the consensus splice-donor site of exon 2 and led to a 70% decrease in NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.
quotes: a 4-bp deletion in intron 2 (IVS2+5_+8delGTAA) of the NDUFV2 gene (encoding NADH dehydrogenase ubiquinone flavoprotein 2) causes complex I deficiency
The homozygous mutation altering the consensus splice-donor site of exon 2 resulted in 70% decreased NDUFV2 protein and complex I deficiency.

relevance_reason: The paper reports NDUFS2 missense mutations in families with complex I deficiency (cardiomyopathy and encephalomyopathy), which is the subject of MC1DN7.

findings.statement: In patients from 3 families with enzymatic complex I deficiency, cardiomyopathy and encephalomyopathy, Loeffen et al. (2001) screened NDUFS2 cDNA by RT-PCR and direct sequencing. They found 3 missense mutations that changed conserved amino acids.
quotes: Screening of patient NDUFS2 cDNA by reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in combination with direct DNA sequencing revealed three missense mutations resulting in the substitution of conserved amino acids in three families.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

findings.statement: Loeffen et al. (2001) noted a high rate of consanguinity and an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance in their group of patients with complex I deficiency. Together with the absence of common mtDNA mutations, this made a nuclear genetic cause likely.
quotes: a high percentage of consanguinity and an autosomal-recessive mode of inheritance observed within our patient group as well as the absence of common mtDNA mutations make a nuclear genetic cause likely.
